regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8%; PMI 54.6","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% looks like acceleration — but IIP overall printed 6.7%, down from 8.8% prior, and core sector slipped to 5.4% from 6.0%, suggesting the headline is flattered by base effects rather than genuine output momentum. PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile) is the more honest signal: services at 54.5 are carrying the load while manufacturing PMI fell to 52.8 from 53.5 — the factory floor is softening even as the services desk stays busy. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up 180bps) is the one number that earns optimism — but it needs to sustain above 78% before private capex commitments follow.","badge_label":"Slowing Pace","badge_type":"b-slow"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 4.45%; Fuel 22.93%","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 4.45% is deceptively calm — the real story is fuel inflation at 22.93% (95th percentile), a 288bps jump in a single month, while core CPI sits at a benign 3.9% (28th percentile). That gap between a commodity-driven spike and subdued core is the trapdoor: if Brent holds above $95, fuel feeds into transport costs, which feeds into food distribution margins, which feeds into CFPI — and the RBI's own revised forecast of 5.1% (up from 4.6%) suggests they already see the transmission risk. Invert the consensus: a 'low core CPI' reading is not a green light for cuts — it is a warning that the next inflation shock will arrive via supply, not demand, and supply shocks are the ones central banks cannot cut their way out of.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 17.1%; CD 81.4%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 17.1% YoY against deposit growth of 10.8% — a 630bps divergence — has pushed the CD ratio to 81.4% (75th percentile), even after a marginal dip from 82.5%. NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% signals that wholesale funding channels are being stretched to fill the gap that retail deposits cannot. The last time India's CD ratio sustained above 80% while the repo rate was being held steady was FY14 — within four quarters, the taper tantrum forced an emergency rate response; today's FX reserves are $100bn larger, but the structural deposit shortfall is not self-correcting, and the regulator's next move is more likely a risk-weight circular than a rate cut.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25%","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% with CPI at 4.45% leaves a real rate of approximately 80bps — but against the RBI's own revised inflation forecast of 5.1%, the forward real rate compresses to 15bps, which is insufficient to defend the rupee at 96.15 or to slow credit growth running at 17.1%. RBI's GDP forecast nudged up to 6.7% from 6.6%, which removes any urgency to cut; the more likely policy action is macro-prudential — tighter risk weights on unsecured and NBFC lending — rather than rate movement in either direction. For corporate capex IRRs, a 5.25% repo with fuel-driven inflation re-accelerating means the real borrowing cost is rising even without a rate hike, which is the stealth tightening the market has not priced.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.1%; CU 77.4%","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up 180bps in a single month — is the strongest simultaneous reading of investment intent and utilisation pressure in this cycle. Core sector at 5.4% is the one note of caution: cement, steel, and electricity generation are the honest proxies for ground-level construction activity, and a deceleration from 6.0% suggests the government's budgeted capex is not yet fully translating into physical throughput. The bull case holds only if utilisation crosses 78% and sustains — at that level, private sector capacity addition becomes economically compelled rather than policy-induced.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST 199853; PV 16%","signal_text":"GST at ₹1,99,853 crore is a near-record print — but the YTD base at a 14th-percentile low suggests the comparison is flattering; the more honest read is whether this reflects genuine demand expansion or continued formalization of the informal economy reclassifying existing spend. Passenger vehicle sales at +16% YoY and two-wheeler at +19.7% are the ground-level confirmation that urban and semi-urban discretionary demand is genuinely strong — two-wheelers in particular are the rural-urban bridge indicator, and a 19.7% print suggests the mass market is participating, not just the affluent tier. Credit card growth at 2.3% YoY (down from 5.6%) is the quiet contradiction: if consumption is broad-based, revolving credit should be accelerating, not decelerating — which implies the vehicle sales are being funded by secured auto loans, not unsecured spend, a structurally healthier but more rate-sensitive composition.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 17.1% YoY (Mar 2026) vs deposit growth at 10.8% — a 350bps divergence widening for three consecutive months. CD ratio at 81.4% (down from 82.5% prior month but structurally elevated). NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% YoY, signalling wholesale funding pressure. Credit-to-deposit gap now at 10-year 75th percentile.","implication":"RBI will face mounting pressure to either hike rates (despite inflation pause) or tighten liquidity to rebalance deposits. Banks with CASA ratios below 40% and NBFCs with wholesale funding >30% of liabilities face margin compression and refinancing risk. Overweight private banks with CASA >45% (HDFC, ICICI); underweight PSU banks and shadow lenders dependent on bond markets. Expect RBI to signal tightening in next policy review.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically preceded either rate hikes or liquidity tightening within 2-3 months. Last similar divergence (2022) led to 140bps of RBI tightening over 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Cycle Firing on All Cylinders","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.1% YoY with capacity utilisation at 77.4% (up 180bps from 75.6% prior month). Core sector growth at 5.4% YoY (down from 6.0% but still positive). India GDP FY estimate at 7.7% (80th percentile hi), RBI GDP forecast at 6.7% (76th percentile mid). PMI composite at 54.6 (83rd percentile hi), services PMI at 54.5 (up from 53.3).","implication":"Private capex cycle is self-sustaining. Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Timken, Xylem), industrial automation (Bosch, ABB), and cement (UltraTech, Ambuja). Capacity utilisation at 77.4% leaves room for 3-4 more quarters of capex before hitting 85%+ constraint. Avoid cyclical downside hedges; instead, position for 18-24 month capex upcycle. Public sector capex remains steady; private sector is the growth driver.","pct_10y":74,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 74th percentile has historically preceded 12-18 months of sustained capex growth. Last similar reading (2021-22) led to 24% cumulative capex growth over 18 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"Retail Equity Inflows Hit All-Time High","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,297 Cr (Mar 2026), rising for 2 consecutive months from ₹29,845 Cr. SIP AUM at ₹18.62 Tr (93rd percentile hi), up from ₹16.64 Tr six months ago — 12% growth. SIP accounts at 100.18 Cr (82nd percentile hi). MF AUM at ₹87.08 Tr (86th percentile hi), rising 2 in a row. DII equity net at ₹58,502 Cr (100th percentile hi) — highest on record.","implication":"Retail equity participation is at generational highs. This is a late-cycle signal: affluent households are rotating into equities after years of fixed income. Expect SIP growth to moderate in next 6-9 months as base effects kick in and market volatility rises. Overweight large-cap quality (Nifty 50 constituents with >20% ROE); avoid micro-cap and speculative segments where retail concentration is highest. Monitor SIP account growth vs AUM growth — if accounts grow 25% but AUM grows 40%, it signals ticket size expansion (late-cycle behaviour).","pct_10y":92,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 92nd percentile have historically preceded 6-12 month market consolidation or correction. Last similar reading (2021) preceded 18-month sideways market before 2023 rally.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens RBI Comfort","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile hi), up from 20.05% prior month — a 288bps jump in one month. WPI at 9.92% (67th percentile mid), rising from 9.78%. Brent crude at $98.77/bbl (69th percentile mid), WTI at $95.47/bbl (80th percentile hi). CPI headline at 4.45% (41st percentile lo), but core CPI at 3.9% (28th percentile lo) — inflation is commodity-driven, not demand-driven.","implication":"Fuel inflation is a structural headwind for RBI's inflation target (4% ±2%). If Brent sustains above $100/bbl, CPI will breach 5% within 2 months, forcing RBI to signal rate hikes despite growth moderation. This creates a policy bind: hike rates and risk capex slowdown, or hold and lose credibility. Hedge long-duration bonds; reduce exposure to rate-sensitive sectors (REITs, utilities). Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) as beneficiaries of higher oil prices. Monitor geopolitical risk (Middle East tensions) as tail risk to oil prices.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile has historically preceded RBI rate hikes within 2-3 months. Last similar spike (2022) led to 140bps of tightening over 6 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"watch","title":"Fed Pause Masks Divergence in G4 Policy","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.63% (flat, 67th percentile mid). US 10Y Treasury at 4.94% (down from 5.01%, but 89th percentile hi) — yields remain elevated despite Fed pause. BOJ rate at 1.0% (up from 0.75%, 86th percentile hi) — first hike in 17 years. ECB deposit rate at 2.25% (up from 2.0%, 59th percentile mid). US PMI composite at 56.0 (84th percentile hi), but US GDP SAAR at 1.5% (down from 2.1%, 49th percentile mid) — growth slowing despite strong PMI.","implication":"G4 policy divergence is creating carry trade unwind risk. BOJ tightening + elevated US yields + ECB holding = yen weakness reversing, dollar strength persisting. This is a headwind for EM currencies (INR, BRL, MXN). FII flows to India remain strong (₹29,631 Cr, 83rd percentile hi) but are vulnerable to sudden reversal if US yields spike or yen carry unwinds. Reduce duration risk in INR bonds; hedge FX exposure for dollar-denominated liabilities. Watch for BOJ guidance on further hikes — any signal of 50bps+ tightening will trigger EM outflows.","pct_10y":89,"pct_note":"US 10Y yields at 89th percentile have historically preceded EM currency weakness and FII outflows. Last similar reading (2022) preceded 18-month period of EM underperformance.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"risk","title":"INR Weakness Accelerates Despite Strong Flows","data_text":"INR/USD at 96.15 (up from 95.86, 91st percentile hi) — weakening for 3 of last 5 observations. DXY at 100.215 (flat, 51st percentile mid) but rising 3 of last 5 observations. FII equity net at ₹29,631 Cr (83rd percentile hi), yet INR still depreciating — suggests RBI is intervening to slow depreciation. India VIX at 11.385 (6th percentile lo, strong-positive signal) — complacency in INR volatility despite FX stress.","implication":"RBI is burning reserves to defend INR at 96 levels. If FII flows reverse (likely if US yields spike or EM risk-off triggers), INR will breach 97-98 rapidly. Current complacency (VIX at 6th percentile) masks tail risk. Reduce long INR positions; hedge dollar liabilities. Monitor RBI's forward guidance on intervention — any signal of reduced support will trigger sharp depreciation. Overweight dollar-denominated assets (US equities, USD bonds) as hedge. Watch for RBI to signal INR weakness acceptance in next policy review.","pct_10y":91,"pct_note":"INR at 91st percentile weakness has historically preceded 6-12 month period of sustained depreciation. Last similar reading (2022) preceded 15% depreciation over 12 months.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Decoupling From IT Stocks","data_text":"Office absorption at 21.5 mn sqft (15th percentile lo, strong-negative signal of -70), yet office vacancy at 13.9% (38th percentile lo, neutral). Rent growth in Mumbai at ₹174/sqft (70th percentile mid, mild-positive +40) and Bengaluru at ₹102/sqft (58th percentile mid, neutral +16). Nifty IT index flat YTD despite office absorption weakness. Bank Nifty at 56,358.7 (93rd percentile hi, strong-positive +86). Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% (35th percentile lo, mild-positive +30).","implication":"Office absorption is collapsing (21.5 mn sqft is 15th percentile — worst in 10 years) but rents are rising and vacancy is stable. This is a GCC (Global Capability Centre) story, not traditional IT services. Multinational tech companies (Google, Microsoft, Amazon) are consolidating into premium Grade-A buildings in Bangalore and Mumbai, while traditional IT services (TCS, Infosys, Wipro) are shedding space. Commercial real estate is decoupling from IT stock performance. This signals: (1) IT services are in structural decline (automation, AI), (2) GCCs are the real growth driver in India's tech ecosystem, (3) office REITs (Embassy, Mindspace) are exposed to wrong tenant mix. Underweight traditional IT services; overweight GCC-exposed real estate and staffing (Kforce, Apex Group). Avoid office REITs until tenant mix shifts to GCCs.","pct_10y":15,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 15th percentile has historically preceded 18-24 month period of REIT underperformance and IT services margin compression. Last similar reading (2020) preceded 3-year period of IT services stock underperformance vs broader market.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

7.8% GDP growth with a 5.1% RBI inflation forecast revision is not a comfortable combination — it is a policy trap. IIP overall at 6.7% (down from 8.8%) and core sector at 5.4% (down from 6.0%) confirm that the headline GDP is running ahead of physical output proxies by a margin that warrants scrutiny of the deflator. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% — up 180bps — is the one structural positive: it is approaching the threshold where private capex becomes self-sustaining rather than policy-dependent. Two-wheeler sales at +19.7% and PV at +16% confirm mass-market consumption is real, but credit card growth decelerating to 2.3% from 5.6% signals the spending is secured, not leveraged — rate-sensitive, not rate-immune.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US 10Y at 4.94% — down 7bps from 5.01% but still at an 89th-percentile yield after rising for five consecutive observations — is the single most important external variable for India's cost of capital and FII allocation calculus. US GDP SAAR at 1.5% (down from 2.1%) while US PMI composite hits 56.0 (84th percentile) is the classic late-cycle divergence: activity surveys lead, hard data lags, and the bond market at 4.94% is pricing the hard data, not the survey. BOJ at 1.0% — a 25bps hike — is unwinding the last pillar of global carry, and with the ECB at 2.25% (up from 2.0%), G4 policy is simultaneously tightening for the first time since 2007 — a configuration that historically precedes EM capital flow reversals within two to three quarters.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

DII equity net at ₹58,502 crore — a 100th-percentile all-time high — and SIP inflows at ₹32,297 crore (rising for two consecutive months) are providing a domestic liquidity floor that is absorbing FII positioning without market dislocation. Yet INR at 96.15 (91st percentile) is weakening despite this flow strength — which means RBI is intervening to slow depreciation, consuming reserves rather than allowing the exchange rate to clear. India VIX at 11.385 (6th percentile) reflects complacency that is inconsistent with a currency at a decade-high stress level and fuel inflation at a 95th-percentile print — the options market is mispricing tail risk by at least one standard deviation. Bank credit at 17.1% against deposit growth of 10.8% means the domestic liquidity engine is running on a structurally thinning fuel base.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 56,358 (93rd percentile) is pricing a credit upcycle — but a CD ratio at 81.4% and NBFC credit growth accelerating to 14.9% from 10.6% sets up a macro-prudential response that would compress NIMs and trigger earnings downgrades across the financial sector. Office REITs are the sharpest contradiction in today's data: Embassy, Mindspace, and Brookfield are all down 16–23% from prior levels while office absorption at 21.5 mn sqft (15th percentile) remains structurally weak — the REIT market is not pricing a recovery, it is pricing a prolonged IT-sector demand drought. Nifty 50 at 23,346 (75th percentile) with India VIX at a 6th-percentile low is a setup where the index is priced for calm that the macro data does not support — any fuel-driven CPI surprise above 5% would reprice both the rate path and equity multiples simultaneously.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three risks, ranked by probability × impact: first, fuel inflation at 22.93% feeding into CPI above 5.1% — the RBI's own revised ceiling — which would force a hawkish pivot and compress the real rate buffer to zero, triggering INR depreciation beyond 97 and a Bank Nifty derating; second, the CD ratio at 81.4% sustaining above 80% for a third consecutive quarter, prompting a risk-weight tightening circular that slows NBFC credit growth from 14.9% and stalls the consumption cycle that two-wheeler and PV sales are currently confirming; third, US 10Y holding above 4.9% while BOJ continues hiking — the carry unwind accelerates, FII equity flows reverse from the current ₹29,631 crore net positive, and DII absorption at record levels proves insufficient to prevent a 5–7% Nifty correction. Watch Friday's US PCE print — if core PCE moves above 3.5%, the Fed pause narrative breaks and every EM rate assumption resets.

"}
